heroHeadline: Senate Confirms $71.7B ICE Reconciliation Floor Vote Week of May 18; Midwest Communities Mobilize Rapid-Response Networks as Enforcement Arrests Surge 30%+
heroSubtitle: Senate Republican leadership confirmed May 11, 2026 that a floor vote on the $71.7 billion immigration enforcement reconciliation bill will occur during the week of May 18, with committee markups scheduled for May 19 — putting Trump's June 1 signing deadline within reach. ICE alone would receive approximately $38.2 billion under the bill, roughly 8× its FY2024 budget, enabling expansion to 100,000+ detention beds and thousands of new agents. Concurrently, KCUR (NPR) documented on May 11 that ICE arrests have surged more than 30% across Iowa, Missouri, Kansas, Oklahoma, and Texas since the Trump second term began — Iowa alone recorded 1,500+ arrests in the past year, exceeding the entire three-year Biden period combined. Grassroots rapid-response networks have emerged across the Midwest: Sioux City's Siouxland Guardians (30+ volunteers), the Western Illinois Dreamers (five-city legal and mental health network), and Oklahoma City's church-based immigration center. USCIS Policy Memorandum PM-602-0198, which ended automatic deportation protection for approximately 200,000 Special Immigrant Juveniles, took effect May 10; A.C.R. v. Noem continues in the Eastern District of New York. Acting ICE Director Todd Lyons remains in post until his May 31 resignation with no successor announced. The Office of Immigration Detention Ombudsman (OIDO) remains closed after its May 5 shutdown, with FY2026 custody deaths at 30+ — record pace. The $71.7B bill includes no independent oversight provisions, minimum medical care standards, or accountability mechanisms for the record death toll.
footerNote: Data sourced from DHS, ICE official records, ACLU, HRW, DHS OIG, TRAC Reports, Detention Watch Network, USCIS, ILRC, NIPNLG, court records, and Congressional records
